records.title: 高空迅速减压飞行人员的临床诊治和医学鉴定
records.locator: Author abstract in original Chinese, Methods and Results (1), article pp. 130–134
records.note: Five selected in-flight decompression incidents, 19 person-exposures. The reported exposure altitude range is 8,300–10,000 m. Exact dates, cabin pressure and gas histories, individual linkage and uniform clinical follow-up are unavailable in the public abstract. The groups differ by incident and reported post-landing management.

observations.group_management: Post-landing rest with oxygen and hyperbaric treatment were not provided in the source's initial grouping.
observations.locator: Author abstract in original Chinese, Methods and Results (1), article pp. 130–134
observations.note: Seven cases explicitly classified as Type II. The abstract does not enumerate other possible clinical diagnoses.

observations.group_management: The group received resting oxygen and referral for hyperbaric oxygen after landing.
observations.locator: Author abstract in original Chinese, Methods and Results (1), article pp. 130–134
observations.note: The original Chinese abstract explicitly states that none developed altitude DCS. The English machine translation omits that sentence.

records.locator: Author abstract, Methods and Results, published pp. 11–12
records.note: The abstract gives return-to-flight status for 19 pilot records across five in-flight incidents. One record involved disqualification for severe psychological symptoms. It supplies no separate DCS case count or DCS-specific return-to-flight denominator.
